title: Leveraging Vision-Language Models for Improving Domain Generalization in Image Classification
authors: S. Addepalli; A. R. Asokan; L. Sharma; R. V. Babu
venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
arch_detail: Student ViT-B/16 ImageNet-1K init; teacher CLIP ViT-B/16 (VLM); VL2V-ADiP align-distill-predict
train_data_note: DomainBed DG benchmarks: OfficeHome, PACS, VLCS, TerraIncognita, DomainNet; 5000 iters (15000 DN), Adam lr 5e-5
train_regime_other: black-box VLM distillation (align, distill, predict) + fine-tuning
effect_size_notes: Avg-OOD reported across DG benchmarks; per-benchmark in sub_experiments
schema_coherence_notes: No schema coherence proxy; representation alignment between VLM and student is measured via distillation losses
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures OOD (domain) generalization gap in image classification and tests an intervention (VLM distillation) that improves OOD accuracy while retaining ID performance; measures one sigma-trap component but does not address flatness, schema coherence, or compositional failure.
relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment framing; robust OOD generalization in a safety-adjacent sense (deployment under distribution shift) but not connected to alignment failure or goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: Assumes black-box access to VLM teacher; gains depend on teacher quality; tested on image classification only; fixed seed 0 for main results with 3 re-runs for a subset.
notes: Avg-ID 73.97, Avg-OOD 75.48 (Table 3, fixed seed 0); DG benchmark average

title: Rethinking Graph Generalization through the Lens of Sharpness-Aware Minimization
authors: Qiu, Y.; Zou, Y.; Wang, J.
venue: WWW 2026 - Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026
arch_detail: Graph Neural Network for graph classification; cVAE-based energy perturbation for OOD augmentation (E2A)
train_data_note: GraphOOD (Motif, CMNIST, HIV, SST2, Twitter) and DrugOOD (EC50, IC50); domain/size-based OOD splits; ROC-AUC or accuracy metric
augmentation_type: energy-guided latent perturbation generating pseudo-OOD samples (E2A)
effect_size_notes: Per-dataset OOD results in sub_experiments; ERM highest ID accuracy but sharp OOD drop (MSF phenomenon)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level schema coherence proxy; sharpness/flatness of loss landscape studied theoretically (SAM lens) but not measured on representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly tests a sigma-targeting intervention family: links sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) theory to OOD generalization in GNNs, proposes flat-minima-seeking energy-based augmentation (E2A), and evaluates OOD performance across 13 graph benchmarks; measures flatness/sharpness but not schema coherence as mediator.
relevance_alignment_justification: No explicit alignment/safety framing; graph OOD generalization motivation is web/graph applications; flatness and robustness discussion is safety-adjacent only.
limitations_text: Authors note E2A requires no environment labels but shows smaller gains on some real-world datasets; theoretical link relies on local first-order approximation assumptions.

title: COGS: A Compositional Generalization Challenge Based on Semantic Interpretation
authors: Najoung Kim; Tal Linzen
arch_detail: Transformer 2 enc+dec layers, 4 heads, FFN 512, 9.5M params; LSTM and BiLSTM encoders 10-11M params; OpenNMT
train_data_note: COGS semantic parsing dataset, fragment of English; training/eval sets differ systematically (structural gaps)
effect_size_notes: Benchmark paper; gap = ID - OOD accuracy
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy
relevance_sigma_justification: Introduces a benchmark directly measuring compositional generalization failure (ID near-perfect vs OOD 16-35%) across Transformer and LSTM architectures with seed sensitivity; measures a core sigma-trap component without connecting to training dynamics or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety or alignment; semantic parsing benchmark only.
limitations_text: COGS covers a fragment of English (small grammar); only seq2seq semantic parsing tested; authors note limitations of the dataset in capturing full natural language compositionality.
open_questions_text: Whether architectural or training modifications improve compositional generalization; which structural properties of training data matter.

title: Measuring Compositional Generalization: A Comprehensive Method on Realistic Data
authors: Daniel Keysers; Nathanael Schärli; Nathan Scales; Hylke Buisman; Daniel Furrer; Sergii Kashubin; Nikola Momchev; Danila Sinopalnikov; Lukasz Stafiniak; Tibor Tihon; Dmitry Tsarkov; Xiao Wang; Marc van Zee; Olivier Bousquet
arch_detail: 3 baseline seq2seq archs: LSTM+attention (Bahdanau), Transformer, Universal Transformer; tensor2tensor defaults
train_data_note: CFQ: 239,357 question-answer pairs over Freebase; MCD splits maximize compound divergence
effect_size_notes: Benchmark paper; gap captured via id_ood_gap_raw
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; DBCA operates on data splits, not internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures one component of the sigma-trap (compositional generalization failure / OOD gap) across three architectures and introduces compound divergence as an OOD difficulty metric, but does not connect to training dynamics, flatness, or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a benchmark construction and evaluation paper.
limitations_text: CFQ is restricted to Freebase QA over English; SPARQL answers anonymized; benchmark covers a single semantic-parsing-style task; authors note the method does not prescribe what distribution a learner should optimize for.
open_questions_text: Apply DBCA to other domains (e.g., visual reasoning based on CLEVR); explore whether improved architectures such as syntactic attention can achieve high accuracy at high compound divergence.
notes: ID = Random split 97.4 +/-0.3 (95% CI); OOD = MCD mean 14.9 +/-1.1 (95% CI), 5 seeds

title: A Benchmark for Systematic Generalization in Grounded Language Understanding
authors: Laura Ruis; Jacob Andreas; Marco Baroni; Diane Bouchacourt; Brenden M. Lake
arch_detail: Baseline: seq2seq with biLSTM command encoder, CNN state encoder, LSTM decoder with double attention; GECA compositional method as comparison
train_data_note: gSCAN grid-world grounded language task; splits A-I covering novel compositions, relativity, adverbs, length
effect_size_notes: Benchmark paper; per-split accuracy in sub_experiments
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy
repr_analysis_finding: Attention analysis shows model fails to attend correctly to target when compositionality required (e.g., 'red squares' split), consistent with systematic generalization failure
relevance_sigma_justification: Introduces a benchmark that directly measures compositional (systematic) generalization failure in grounded language understanding across multiple OOD split types; measures a central sigma-trap component but does not connect to training dynamics, flatness, or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety or alignment; grounded language benchmark only.
limitations_text: Authors note the benchmark covers a subset of systematic generalization (grounded language in a synthetic grid world); agent receives symbolic world representation rather than raw images.
open_questions_text: Whether models with stronger compositional inductive biases (e.g., GECA) generalize better on relational splits; extension to richer visual input.
